results.explanation: At POST /process/file, the non-admin source-file lookup uses the caller's user ID, so the visible check concerns ownership or visibility of the supplied file, not permission to write to the destination collection. The supplied collection name is bound to collection_name and, when no direct content is supplied, file-derived content is placed in docs. The protected write path is the call to save_docs_to_vector_db with those docs and the caller-selected collection_name, using add=True when a collection name was supplied. The supplied fixed-source crop does not contain save_docs_to_vector_db or the omitted dependency locations, so it does not establish whether that sink performs the write or whether destination ownership or an explicit destination write grant is enforced before it. The visible _validate_collection_access helper defaults to read access, and its invocation from process_file is not shown. Therefore the source-visible authorization outcome at the declared boundary is unknown rather than a proven allow or deny.

async def _validate_collection_access(collection_names: list[str], user, access_type: str = 'read') -> None:
    """
    Raise 403 if the user lacks access to any of the requested collections.
    Delegates to the shared filter_accessible_collections utility so the
    access rules stay in one place.
    """
    requested = set(collection_names)
    allowed = await filter_accessible_collections(requested, user, access_type=access_type)
    denied = requested - allowed
    if denied:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
        )
